title: Copilot Studio: MCP servers as tools in workflow agent nodes
summary: Hold: the briefing understates the documented reach of connector policies and overstates when workflows incur credits. Microsoft documents policy enforcement for Copilot Studio agents and a licensing exception for workflows run inside a standard harness agent by a licensed user. The cited admin paths and API operations were confirmed, including both endpoints flagged by the pre-check.

claims.claim: The agent node page does not specify which identity an MCP tool call uses.
claims.quote: Searched: '"agent node" "MCP" "identity"'; opened agent-node-workflow and tools-add-mcp-server. The former specifies Work IQ's running-user context but not the identity used for MCP tool calls; the latter describes server-dependent authentication outside the node.

claims.claim: The agent node page does not document adding a custom MCP server URL from the node.
claims.quote: Searched: '"agent node" "custom" "URL" MCP'; opened agent-node-workflow and tools-add-mcp-server. The node page documents tool selection, not URL entry; the other page documents a custom-URL path on an agent's Build tab, not in the workflow node.

claims.where: controls[0].governs; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance
claims.claim: ACP supports blocking an entire MCP server.
claims.quote: Within advanced connector policies, administrators can see MCP servers listed alongside other connector types and can choose to block an entire MCP server.

claims.claim: ACP does not currently offer granular blocking of individual tools within an MCP server.
claims.quote: As of now, granular control over individual MCP tools (endpoints and actions) within an MCP server isn't available. Blocking the entire MCP server is supported.

claims.claim: Saving a single-environment ACP policy immediately blocks connectors not explicitly allowed.
claims.quote: ACP enforces a strict allowlist as soon as you save it (single environment) or publish it (environment group): every connector that isn't explicitly allowed is blocked.

claims.claim: New connectors are blocked by default under ACP.
claims.quote: New connectors added to the platform are automatically blocked.

claims.claim: In mixed mode, ACP and classic data policies run together and enforce the most restrictive settings.
claims.quote: Mixed mode (default): ACP runs alongside classic data policies, and the most restrictive settings from both are enforced.

claims.claim: The ACP documentation places Copilot Studio design-time enforcement after Power Automate in the rollout order.
claims.quote:
Design-time enforcement is rolling out across maker portals in the following order:

1. Power Automate maker portal — rolling out first
2. Copilot Studio — following Power Automate

claims.claim: ACP enforcement is runtime-only for a workload until its maker portal has design-time support.
claims.quote: Until design-time support is available in a given maker portal, ACP operates as a runtime-only enforcement for that workload.

claims.claim: Blocking Power Platform connectors in data policies also blocks tools in connected MCP servers that rely on them.
claims.quote: Blocking Power Platform connectors also blocks access to tools in connected MCP servers, which rely on Power Platform connectors for connectivity.

claims.claim: The data-policy page requires a tenant admin or the Environment Admin role.
claims.quote: Be a tenant admin or have the Environment Admin role.

claims.quote: To view credit consumption across an environment or your tenant, go to Licensing > Copilot Studio in the Power Platform admin center.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Governance controls; Open questions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Microsoft has not confirmed that classic data policies apply to MCP tools in the workflow agent node.
claims.quote: These data policies apply to Copilot Studio agents in the environments included in the policy's scope.
claims.fix: Replace the classic-data-policy nonapplicability caveat throughout with: 'Data policies apply to Copilot Studio agents in environments within the policy scope; blocking Power Platform connectors also blocks tools in connected MCP servers that rely on those connectors.' The node documentation explicitly calls its inline component an agent, so a separate node-specific statement is not required by this platform-wide rule. Keep the recommendation to verify the configured policy in development, but remove the assertion that its applicability is undocumented.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Governance controls; Open questions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Microsoft has not confirmed that advanced connector policies govern MCP tools in the workflow agent node.
claims.quote: At runtime, when a connector operation is invoked, it queries the effective policy for the current hosting environment. This query includes a combined policy that merges the most restrictive settings from both classic data policies and ACP to provide full enforcement.
claims.fix: Replace the ACP nonapplicability caveat throughout with: 'ACP governs supported connectors in the hosting environment, including MCP server-level blocking. Copilot Studio design-time enforcement follows Power Automate; until design-time support is available, ACP is runtime-only for that workload.' The cited ACP page documents this platform scope, so do not require a separate statement naming the inline node before acknowledging it. Remove the open question about whether ACP applies at all; retain only uncertainty about the current design-time rollout.

claims.claim: Every workflow run draws on Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: | Workflows | Yes, when run inside a standard harness agent by a licensed user | Billed in all other cases. |
claims.fix: Replace 'makers can start attaching MCP servers, and every run draws on Copilot Credits' with 'makers can start attaching MCP servers, and workflow runs can consume Copilot Credits'. In Cost and licensing add the qualification: 'Microsoft lists workflows run inside a standard harness agent by a licensed user as covered by a Microsoft 365 Copilot licence; workflows are billed in all other cases.' Do not conflate this workflow exception with the separate rule that Microsoft Copilot harness agents are billed for all usage.

claims.claim: ACP supports environment-group scope as well as the single-environment UI identified in the note.
claims.quote: You can configure advanced connector policies at the environment group level for bulk deployment or directly on individual environments for targeted governance.

claims.claim: Data policies can be tenant-scoped.
claims.quote: Policies with a tenant scope apply to all agents in all environments across the tenant.

claims.claim: Credit allocations are environment-scoped and the capacity controls cover workflows, not just agents.
claims.quote: The capacity and consumption controls in the Power Platform admin center apply across Copilot Studio. They aren't exclusive to the Microsoft Copilot harness. Configure controls with the other Copilot Studio agents, workflows, and features in mind for each environment.

claims.where: front matter: cost; rationale: cost; summary
claims.claim: Variable cost is consistent with the documented Copilot Credits meter.
claims.quote: Usage is billed based on consumption and measured in Copilot Credits.
